project.title: Hotel booking prototype
project.alt: Actual hotel demonstration homepage with future date selection and credited illustrative bedroom photography
project.desc: A polished multi-step hotel demonstration with exact pricing, stable confirmation retries and recoverable booking reviews.
project.built: Preserved the established hotel interface and strengthened the shared booking rules and review lifecycle so date changes, expired sessions and repeated confirmations behave predictably.
project.why: A multi-step transaction should carry information reliably from one screen to the next. The project explores session state, validation and pricing across a booking journey.
how: Choose future dates, a room type and quantity; the shared rules calculate an exact integer-cent example total.
Enter sample guest details and review the quote. Changed or expired reviews are refreshed without losing the selection, and require explicit confirmation again.
Complete a demonstration confirmation, revisit it safely or edit dates and review a new quotation; no actual room is reserved.
project.demonstrates: Server-rendered web development, session handling, input validation and turning a multi-step process into a working application.
project.caption: Genuine capture of the verified shared interface. The hotel is fictional; photography is illustrative and credited. Browser-only public mode is labelled prominently.
project.result: Backend/rule regressions, an isolated MySQL 8.4 catalog check and complete browser journeys are required before release. Tests cover simultaneous confirmation identity, review expiry, strict numeric inputs, exact-cent totals, date changes, restored sessions, stale stored prices, reload/reset and mobile layout. The linked run identifies the exact tested revision.
project.limits: The hotel, rooms, prices and guest records are synthetic. Public Pages runs only the shared browser demonstration; it does not run Express or MySQL. Stock is illustrative per room type, not a date-based hotel inventory or a held allocation. Confirmations create no real reservation, payment, account or message. Review/receipt state is temporary; the bounded Express cache and local session store are educational rather than a production booking database.
project.technical: One shared JavaScript rules module serves Express and the static frontend. Rates use positive integer cents within the existing DECIMAL(10,2) catalog range; counts reject coercion and ambiguous numeric syntax. Reviews have a shared 15-minute lifetime. A bounded temporary token-keyed receipt cache keeps concurrent Express retries consistent; browser confirmation reuses the same reviewed receipt. Recovery refreshes session/catalog and review, preserving sample guest details while requiring a new explicit confirmation. CSRF and safe catalog errors remain enforced.
project.run: Run npm ci, npm test and npm start for Express at http://127.0.0.1:3000. No database is needed by default. npm run build:demo generates the public static version. An optional isolated MySQL Docker setup and opt-in integration test are documented separately.
gallery: Synthetic room cards, capacity and quantity remain clearly explained.
Actual Express recovery after its browser session cookies were cleared: sample details are retained and a second confirmation is required.
Exact room × nights × quantity pricing before explicit confirmation.
A genuine demonstration receipt, preserved when the same reviewed quote is confirmed again.
project.challenge: A booking review can outlive its session or price, and two simultaneous requests can otherwise create different confirmation references. The workflow separates a reviewed quote from its immutable receipt: stale reviews are rebuilt for explicit approval, while retries for the same review preserve identity. Date changes invalidate downstream selections and retain reusable guest details.
